title: Performance comparison of retrieval-augmented generation and fine-tuned large language models for construction safety management knowledge retrieval
task: 安全知识检索与预防措施生成
inputData: 事故摘要文本 + 施工安全指南知识图谱/问答数据
contribution: 直接比较面向施工安全知识检索的知识图谱RAG与领域微调LLM：RAG将GPT-4与由安全指南构建的知识图谱结合，微调模型使用同源问答数据训练；两者均较通用GPT-4提升事故案例预防措施生成质量，为RAG与参数内化两类领域适配路线提供了直接对照。
abstract: Construction safety standards are often stored in unstructured text and image documents, limiting their direct use in daily safety management. This study develops and compares two domain-adapted approaches for construction safety knowledge retrieval: a retrieval-augmented generation model integrating GPT-4 with a knowledge graph derived from construction safety guidelines, and a fine-tuned LLM trained on a question-answering dataset derived from the same guidelines. Accident synopses are used as case-study queries to generate preventive measures, and the generated responses are compared with reference preventive strategies using cosine similarity, Euclidean distance, BLEU, and ROUGE. Both approaches outperform standard GPT-4, with reported improvements of 21.5% for RAG and 26% for the fine-tuned LLM.
methodology: The study constructs two parallel construction-safety LLM workflows from official safety-guideline documents. In the RAG branch, safety-guideline knowledge is represented as a knowledge graph and supplied to GPT-4 through retrieval. In the fine-tuning branch, question-answer pairs derived from the same guideline source are used to adapt an LLM to construction-safety knowledge. Accident synopses are then submitted as queries and the systems generate preventive measures. The generated outputs are evaluated against preventive measures in official accident-case references using semantic-distance and text-overlap metrics, enabling a controlled comparison of non-parametric retrieval grounding and parameter-based domain adaptation.
results: Both domain-adapted systems outperformed the standard GPT-4 baseline on the construction-safety case studies. The paper reports an overall improvement of 21.5% for the knowledge-graph RAG model and 26% for the fine-tuned LLM, with BLEU, ROUGE, cosine-similarity, and Euclidean-distance evaluations showing improved relevance and keyword-level agreement with reference preventive measures. The comparison also highlights different trade-offs between dynamic knowledge retrieval and knowledge internalization through fine-tuning.
taskEn: Construction safety knowledge retrieval and preventive-measure generation
inputDataEn: Accident synopsis text plus construction-safety guideline knowledge graph / QA data
operationEvidence: The RAG branch retrieves construction-safety guideline knowledge from an explicit knowledge graph, while both evaluated systems generate preventive measures for accident synopses and compare those recommendations with official reference measures.
